<p class="print-note">Eight claims, each broken in a different way. Cut along
the dashed lines and deal one per team. Page&nbsp;2 is the diagnosis sheet.</p>

<div class="sheetwrap">
<div class="cards">

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 1</span>
    <h3>Breakfast</h3>
    <p class="claim">"Students who eat breakfast score higher. Schools should serve breakfast."</p>
    <p class="who">A school district, proposing a budget line</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Diagnose</b> using this morning's vocabulary. Draw it.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 2</span>
    <h3>The consultants</h3>
    <p class="claim">"Firms that hire consultants grow faster than firms that don't. So hire consultants."</p>
    <p class="who">A consulting firm's own marketing deck</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Diagnose</b> using this morning's vocabulary. Draw it.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 3</span>
    <h3>The hiring puzzle</h3>
    <p class="claim">"Among the people we hired, the ones with the best test scores had the worst interviews. Our test must be measuring the wrong thing."</p>
    <p class="who">A head of recruiting, about to scrap the test</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Diagnose.</b> This one is not what it looks like.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 4</span>
    <h3>The loyalty app</h3>
    <p class="claim">"Customers on our app spend 40% more. Getting the other half onto the app would raise revenue 40%."</p>
    <p class="who">A retailer's board paper</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Diagnose</b> using this morning's vocabulary. Draw it.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 5</span>
    <h3>The promotion gap</h3>
    <p class="claim">"Once we control for salary band, the gender gap in promotion disappears. So there is no bias in promotion."</p>
    <p class="who">An HR review, closing the matter</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Diagnose.</b> Controlling for the wrong thing is also a mistake.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 6</span>
    <h3>The founders</h3>
    <p class="claim">"Nine of the ten most valuable startups were founded by people who dropped out. Dropping out is an advantage."</p>
    <p class="who">A widely shared post</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Diagnose.</b> Who is missing from this comparison?</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 7</span>
    <h3>The turnaround team</h3>
    <p class="claim">"We send the turnaround team to our worst-performing stores. Those stores improve. The programme works."</p>
    <p class="who">An operations VP, requesting more budget</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Diagnose.</b> What would have happened anyway?</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 8</span>
    <h3>The crime wave</h3>
    <p class="claim">"Reported cybercrime doubled after 2019. Cybercrime is out of control."</p>
    <p class="who">A vendor selling security software</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Diagnose.</b> What changed besides the world?</p>
  </div>

</div>

<div class="pagebreak"></div>

<div class="defence">
  <h3>Diagnosis sheet — team <span style="color:#b31b1b">______</span> &nbsp;·&nbsp; card <span style="color:#b31b1b">____</span></h3>

  <p class="lbl" style="margin-top:0.1in">How this runs</p>
  <p class="vocab" style="font-style:normal">Every team works its card at
  the same time. Then <b>one team is drawn at random</b> to defend at the
  front while everyone else attacks — and we draw again, and again. You
  will not know whether you are up, so be ready. <b>Points for an attack
  that lands</b>, and you have to name what is wrong, not just dislike it.</p>

  <p class="lbl">The graph behind the claim — draw it</p>
  <div class="big"></div>

  <p class="vocab">Name it with the vocabulary: <b>confounder</b> ·
  <b>collider</b> · <b>mediator</b> · <b>selection</b> ·
  <b>reverse causality</b> · <b>survivorship</b> ·
  <b>regression to the mean</b> · <b>the measure changed</b></p>

  <p class="lbl">What is actually wrong here</p>
  <div class="row"></div>

  <p class="lbl">What would you have to condition on — and what must you leave alone?</p>
  <div class="row"></div>

  <p class="lbl">What comparison would settle it, if you could run any study you liked?</p>
  <div class="row"></div>

  <p class="lbl">From the floor: the objection that landed</p>
  <div class="row"></div>
</div>
</div>
